$schema: Session state manifest v3 - vertical phase slices, programmatic updates only
description: Migrate the demo suite from hand-wired pages into a scene composition system where each page (title screen, main menu, etc.) is a scene composed of typed asset layers (fonts, backgrounds, effects, media).

data.topic_summary: Migrate hand-wired Vite pages into a scene composition system where scenes correspond to pages (title, menu, etc.) and are built from typed reusable asset layers.

key_decisions.title: Scene = Page (Unity Scene model)
key_decisions.rationale: Each scene is one full stage, 1:1 with a web page. Assets are placed into scenes. System targets landing pages / static websites, not interactive applications.

key_decisions.title: Dual-surface authoring (visual editor + agent API)
key_decisions.rationale: Human authors via visual canvas editor with drag-and-drop and property panels. AI agent edits programmatically via API on the same scene data. Generalizes the pattern already proven in the melee-3 font app.

key_decisions.title: Collapsible group layer model (tree hierarchy)
key_decisions.rationale: Scene layers form a tree, not a flat stack. Complex assets like the CodeCaine logo are groups that expand to reveal sub-layers with configurable properties. Sub-layers can reference other assets (e.g. video). Other scene assets can interleave between a group's sub-layers. Like Photoshop layer groups or Unity Hierarchy.

key_decisions.title: Full replacement of apps/frontend/
key_decisions.rationale: Scene system replaces the existing frontend entirely. All pages rebuilt as scenes. Everything unified into one application.

key_decisions.title: Option A — content separate, assets reusable
key_decisions.rationale: Assets live in registry as reusable building blocks. Content lives with components. Scenes are lean composition manifests referencing assets by ID. Avoids duplication, keeps editor focused on visual composition.

key_decisions.title: Scene data format confirmed (scene.json)
key_decisions.rationale: JSON with id, name, stage dimensions, and layers array. Layer types: media, effect, glyph-group, component. Groups use children array for sub-layers with interleaving support. Z-order is array position (last on top). Both editor and agent operate on this format.

key_decisions.title: Font pipeline stays separate, editor app absorbed
key_decisions.rationale: Python pipeline is an asset factory — stays in apps/font-creation/. The melee-3 Vite editor app's layer editing capabilities get folded into the scene editor as the glyph-group property inspector. One editor, not two.

key_decisions.title: Five asset types on day one
key_decisions.rationale: All five needed for the title scene vertical slice: glyph-group, media, effect, component, audio.

commits.message: checkpoint-1: Stand up scene-engine tracer bullet
checkpoint-2: Asset registry + glyph-group renderer + CODECAINE logo
checkpoint-3: Group children — sub-layer overrides + foreign-asset interleaving
checkpoint-5: Editor authoring — drag, edit, reorder, save
checkpoint-6: Component + audio assets, full title scene, multi-page build, retire apps/frontend/
